scenes.text: Imagine standing deep inside a massive, beautiful national park, knowing you could commit a serious crime in one specific spot of forest and completely get away with it legally.

In Yellowstone National Park, there is a remote fifty mile strip of land famously called the Zone of Death where a bizarre constitutional loophole makes criminal prosecution practically impossible to carry out.
Because the local district court boundaries overlap multiple states, any criminal trial here legally requires a jury of local residents from an area where absolutely nobody actually lives.

Since the government cannot physically form a jury, this mind-blowing legal loophole remains completely active today, so would you ever dare to camp in this lawless territory? Comment your thoughts below and follow for more insane historical facts!
